producer_report.summary: Added a "Crate reach" bullet to docs/system-facts.md. It says only cli has a binary, xtask has no library target and xtask code is tested in xtask/tests/ or unit tests in xtask/src/, and it gives one `- crate <name>: lib|bin|lib+bin; deps ...; dev ...` line per workspace crate. Added a ninth, prose-only "Test placement" line to READING_RULES. Added a drift test in budgets.rs that computes the crate lines from the Cargo.toml files and the src layout, and rejects a doctored, missing, unknown, repeated or malformed line. The facts-file test now has 5 more markers and expects at least 12 bullets. The reading-rules section cap went from 2600 to 2750 bytes. The facts file is 4990 bytes, under the 5,000 cap. Root cause: nothing the reader or planner saw said which crates have libraries or may depend on which, so a test could be placed where the code cannot be imported. The failure-class merge is left to the user because it lives in records/. Everything I ran passed (see checks_run).

The facts file is 4990 bytes, 10 under the cap. To fit, I shortened two existing clauses in the new bullet's neighbours: the Early-wait bullet now ends 'to reuse its pass' (was 'so the landing run finds the cached pass'). The next fact added to the file will need further trimming or a cap discussion.
The reading-rules section size before the new line (about 2540) is an estimate (2718 measured after, minus the new line's length); the CHANGELOG and the code comment say 'about'.
mistakes: My first draft of the Crate reach prose pushed the facts file to 5105 bytes, then 5030 after a first trim. I shortened the prose and one clause of the Early-wait bullet to reach 4990.
learnings: Only athena-cli has a [[bin]]; every package under crates/ has src/lib.rs; xtask has only src/main.rs plus modules ci_cache, decisions, shard, site and walltime, so unit tests there live in xtask/src/ and integration tests in xtask/tests/.
The toml crate is already a dependency of athena-cli, so the drift test parses Cargo.toml files with it and Cargo.lock does not change.
The facts-file test splits bullets on "\n- **", so nested two-space-indented `- crate` lines stay inside their bullet.
Bash allows no pipes or tail here, so cargo output is read in full; `cargo test -p <crate> --lib -- <filter1> <filter2>` runs several test filters in one go.
The 'Reading rules' section measured 2718 bytes with nine rules (cap now 2750).
desires: A way to run the facts-file size check directly, without a failing test, to read the byte count.
